candidate_profile.description: The candidate recognizes that the route should be evaluated on profitability and mentions demand and cost, but the logic is shallow and cannibalization is either underweighted or poorly handled.
behaviour_rules: Recognize that the route should make money, but do not build a very clean structure around it.
Ask some useful questions on demand or costs, but not in a disciplined sequence.
Mention occupancy and pricing, but do not clearly connect them to competitive dynamics.
Acknowledge operating costs such as fuel, but underdevelop landing rights and other incremental route costs.
Notice cannibalization, but discuss it only briefly or treat it too simplistically.
Fail to articulate clearly that the right metric is incremental profit after cannibalization.
Give a recommendation that is directionally reasonable but lacks rigor.

expected_issues: Only partially structures the route decision as incremental profitability.
Does not fully connect occupancy and pricing to demand and competition.
Recommendation is not framed tightly enough around net route economics.
expected_feedback_points: Tie occupancy and pricing explicitly to demand and competitor behavior.
Consider all major incremental costs, not only fuel.
Be explicit that cannibalization reduces net value but may still be strategically acceptable.
Base the recommendation on net incremental profit.
